title: The readback fails any member whose model names a context variant
foundBy: repository owner, on a campaign that would not dispatch: "About claude-opus-5-5[1m], isn't that a valid model name for Claude code to use?"

evidence.verified: `go test ./internal/cli/ -run 'ContextVariant|AssertDeclaredTurnConfig|DeclaredSuffix' -count=1` passes. With the change reverted, the case `a variant is satisfied by its base id` fails with the line the campaign printed: `declared model claude-opus-5-5[1m] but the turn answered on claude-opus-5-5`. The full gate passes on this commit, with the smoke tier included.

resolution: `matches` now takes both what the operator wrote and what a transcript can carry. The two differ only where a declaration names a context window: `contextVariant` splits the bracketed suffix off, and the plain id satisfies the comparison. A failure still quotes the declaration as the operator wrote it. `declaredSuffix` names what the turn could not show, so a passing line no longer claims to cover the suffix. The manual's readback section says the same.
details:
In one campaign the orchestrator's declared model was `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`. `validate` accepted it, `create` provisioned six microVMs, and the readback failed the campaign:

```
BAD readback orchestrator (claude): declared model claude-opus-5-5[1m]
  but the turn answered on claude-opus-5-5 — the declaration did not take
cs-campaign: readback FAILED — 1 member(s) could not confirm their briefing; do not dispatch
```

The declaration had taken. The check cannot see it.

`assertDeclaredTurnConfig` compares the declared string with the models the transcript names, through `matches`, which is a literal `slices.Contains`. The observed list comes from `turnConfigCommand`, which greps `"model":"…"` out of the CLI's JSONL. That field carries the API model id. A bracketed suffix asks Claude Code for a context window and selects the session, not the model, so it never appears there. No member declaring a context variant can pass.

Measured against a session whose model id is `claude-opus-5[1m]`, using the command the check itself runs:

```console
$ set -- "$HOME"/.cs-claude/projects/*/*.jsonl
$ grep -ho '"model":"[^"]*"' "$@" | sed 's/.*:"//;s/"$//' | sort -u
claude-opus-5
claude-opus-5-5
<synthetic>
```

No bracket, in a session that has one.

What it cost: the campaign could not dispatch, and there is no supported way to correct a declaration on an existing campaign. The record holds it, so editing the profile does not reach it and re-running `create` fails identically; `--set` has no `model` path. The fleet was destroyed and recreated on the plain model, which ran the whole campaign on a smaller context window than was asked for.

The validator that admits the token (SAC-064) is right, and so is the manual sentence about what the form means. Only the confirmation is wrong.
